Daily Brief

Ukraine struck a critical blow against Russian logistics by severely damaging the Crimean Bridge in what President Zelensky described as an 'unprecedented operation,' causing a major section to collapse into the water [BBC, Al Jazeera, ABC Australia]. The timing is significant as the strike precedes a rare trilateral summit between Presidents Xi, Trump, and Putin in Shenzhen this week, drawing comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference [Globe and Mail, Nikkei Asia]. Meanwhile, the fallout from the Nvidia scandal continues to shape US-China tech relations, with Washington announcing new restrictions on remote access to AI chips through third-country data centres [The Hindu, Al Jazeera, BBC]. In Europe, five EU member states announced joint negotiations with Rwanda to establish deportation centres for rejected asylum seekers [The Guardian, RFI], while French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen signalled she would end financial aid to Ukraine if elected [RFI]. The Quad leaders met in Manila, unveiling new defence cooperation and critical minerals agreements aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence [ABC Australia, Nikkei Asia, The Hindu].

01 Conflict

Ukraine Inflicts Major Damage on Crimean Bridge in 'Unprecedented' Strike

  • Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, causing a large arched section to collapse into the water
  • President Zelensky said the attack followed weeks of methodically destroying Russian air defences, radar systems, and electronic warfare capabilities
  • Russia's Crimea governor reported two deaths and suspended all traffic across the 19-kilometre road and rail bridge
  • The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed and vowed to rebuild the bridge 'better than before'

US Tightens AI Chip Export Controls Amid Nvidia Scandal Fallout

  • US announced new regulations requiring licences for remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third countries, targeting Chinese firms
  • The rules were written by Treasury and the White House rather than Commerce, reflecting reported tensions between Secretaries Bessent and Lutnick

  • China condemned the restrictions as 'abusing export control measures'; announcement came days before Trump-Xi summit

Five EU States Launch Joint Negotiations with Rwanda for Migrant Deportation Centre

  • Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark, and Greece are negotiating with Rwanda to establish a centre for migrants whose asylum claims have been rejected
  • The pilot scheme would accommodate around 100 adults who have exhausted all legal appeals, excluding minors
  • Unlike the failed UK-Rwanda scheme, this would not apply to people still pursuing asylum claims
  • 45 human rights organisations criticised the plans in a joint letter, while Rwanda's interior minister said it offers migrants a 'second chance'
